## Publication

A. Balaji, **A. Nema**, N. Kamath, and J. Raju. "Encoding Values: Injecting Morality into Machines via Prompt-Conditioned Moral Frames." *NeurIPS 2025 Creative AI Track*. Published on OpenReview.

[Read the OpenReview paper](https://openreview.net/forum?id=gzX840IFM4)

## Summary

This paper explores how moral values can be represented and injected into AI generation through prompt-conditioned moral frames. Instead of aligning models to a single universal policy, the work studies prompt-level moral steering with ten-principle constitutions that reflect different value frames.

The study evaluates seven constitution-style prompt frames across 100 questions and four task types, using four LLMs and metrics covering toxicity, semantic alignment, lexical markers, and LLM-as-a-judge quality. The results show that prompted moral frames can improve alignment and judged quality without increasing toxicity, while placebo prompts do not show the same effect.

## Why It Matters

As large language models become part of everyday decision support, creative workflows, and public-facing tools, value alignment is not just a theoretical concern. This research contributes to the practical question of how systems can be nudged toward more responsible behavior without hiding the intervention inside an opaque pipeline.

## Portfolio Relevance

This work reflects my interest in responsible AI, prompt engineering, and the social impact of machine learning systems. It pairs naturally with my applied AI experience because it asks not only whether an AI system can produce an answer, but what kind of values shape that answer.
